finding_statement: Devanagari spelling errors cause severe target-word subword fragmentation
statistic: +1.00 subwords on average (collapsing single-subword coverage from 90.0% to 30.0% in MuRIL and 70.0% to 20.0% in XLM-RoBERTa)
sample_size_and_denominator: N=20 pairs (20 original and 20 contrast targets)
scientific_interpretation: Devanagari matra inversions and ligature splits destroy common subword vocabulary entries, forcing tokenizers into byte/character fragmentation.
scientific_limitation: N=20 spelling pairs is exploratory; cannot infer exact fragmentation rates across the entire Hindi lexicon.

finding_statement: MuRIL achieves ~12% higher overall tokenization compactness on Hindi text than XLM-RoBERTa
statistic: Mean sentence tokens: 8.95 (MuRIL) vs. 10.19 (XLM-RoBERTa) on standard context track (length ratio: 1.01x vs. 1.02x)
scientific_interpretation: MuRIL's Indic-dedicated vocabulary provides superior native representation of Devanagari characters compared to XLM-RoBERTa's multilingual shared budget.
scientific_limitation: Does not imply superior downstream semantic understanding; only indicates subword segmentation compactness.

finding_statement: Pretrained MLMs reliably prefer canonical Hindi sentences over spelling errors
statistic: Original sentence preferred in 95.0% (19/20) of pairs by MuRIL (mean Δ MeanLogP = -2.0368) and 65.0% (13/20) by XLM-RoBERTa (mean Δ MeanLogP = -0.6695)
scientific_interpretation: Both models assign lower statistical likelihood to orthographic errors; MuRIL demonstrates substantially stronger penalty than XLM-RoBERTa.
scientific_limitation: Pseudo-log-likelihood measures corpus predictability and statistical typicality rather than normative grammatical correctness.

finding_statement: MLMs exhibit minimal score drops on valid Hindi synonym substitutions
statistic: Mean Δ MeanLogP: -0.0655 (XLM-RoBERTa) and -0.5810 (MuRIL); original preferred in only 57.9% and 84.2% of pairs
scientific_interpretation: Pretrained models treat valid Hindi synonyms as substantially interchangeable relative to spelling errors or contextual mismatches.
scientific_limitation: Score differences between synonyms often reflect word-frequency differences in the pretraining corpora rather than semantic divergence.

finding_statement: Cross-model direction agreement is moderate overall but collapses on synonyms
statistic: 74.5% overall direction agreement (Spearman rs = +0.4408; p < 10^-9); collapses to 57.9% on synonyms (rs = +0.0595; p = 0.7226)
scientific_interpretation: The models share broad sensitivity patterns for obvious errors and contextual contrasts but diverge when evaluating near-equivalent lexical alternatives.
scientific_limitation: Rank correlation is moderate; ~45% of variance is shared between models.

finding_statement: Attention explanations exhibit 2x to 3x higher rank stability than Integrated Gradients under spelling noise
statistic: Mean visible-target Spearman rho: 0.7425 vs. 0.3589 in XLM-RoBERTa; 0.7043 vs. 0.2632 in MuRIL
sample_size_and_denominator: N=20 pairs per model; pooled all-scorable
model_method_track: MuRIL and XLM-RoBERTa; Attention vs. IG; REALISTIC_SPELLING_ERROR
scientific_interpretation: Last-layer self-attention routing across unperturbed context tokens is robust to target spelling noise; IG token-gradient rankings are volatile.
scientific_limitation: IG cosine similarity remains high (0.899–0.988); gradients retain overall orientation but relative token rankings fluctuate.

finding_statement: Stage 6 masked-target protocol induced an experimental artifact yielding illusory perfect stability
statistic: Spearman rho = 1.0000; Cosine Sim = 1.0000; Delta Logit = 0.0 with zero variance across all pairs
sample_size_and_denominator: N=20 pairs (6 MuRIL / 4 XLM-R strict single-subword)
model_method_track: MuRIL and XLM-RoBERTa; Stage 6 Masked-Target Protocol
scientific_interpretation: Masking the target word in both sentences removed the perturbation itself, resulting in byte-identical input sequences.
scientific_limitation: Resolved in Stage 7 via the Visible-Target Scoring Protocol; must be explicitly documented as an artifact.

finding_statement: Attention outperforms Integrated Gradients in discrete token erasure faithfulness
statistic: Win rate vs. bottom-k control: 75.0%–77.5% for Attention in XLM-RoBERTa (Gap: +4.02 to +5.17) vs. 50.0%–60.0% for IG (Gap: +1.84 to +3.30)
sample_size_and_denominator: N=40 sentence evaluations per condition (20 pairs x 2 sentences)
model_method_track: MuRIL and XLM-RoBERTa; Attention vs. IG; REALISTIC_SPELLING_ERROR
scientific_interpretation: Attention attributions track discrete token importance more reliably than IG continuous path integrals under MLM context erasure.
scientific_limitation: Erasure via [MASK] creates out-of-distribution sequences; attention is non-causal and reflects correlation rather than proven mechanism.

finding_statement: Context masking in XLM-RoBERTa produces counter-intuitive target logit inflation
statistic: Mean top drop = -7.1884; bottom drop = -11.2055 (target logits increased after masking)
scientific_interpretation: Directional faithfulness is preserved because bottom-k increased logits more than top-k (Gap = (-7.19) - (-11.21) = +4.02), but raw drop is negative.
scientific_limitation: MLM perplexity shock and unnormalized logit dynamics distort absolute scale; relative comparisons remain valid.

finding_statement: Explanation stability under spelling noise does not predict masking-based faithfulness
statistic: Spearman rs = +0.2704 (p = 0.2490) in XLM-R Attention; rs = -0.1611 (p = 0.4974) in MuRIL Attention; rs = +0.1583 (p = 0.5052) in XLM-R IG; rs = +0.0075 (p = 0.9749) in MuRIL IG
model_method_track: MuRIL and XLM-RoBERTa; Attention & IG; REALISTIC_SPELLING_ERROR
scientific_interpretation: Attribution stability and intervention faithfulness represent orthogonal dimensions of explanation quality; stability cannot serve as a proxy for faithfulness.
scientific_limitation: N=20 has limited power to detect small effect sizes (|r| < 0.30); does not prove zero correlation in all possible domains.
